about: Written by demo/public-run for its run on chain 421614, from public-arbitrum-sepolia.json. The addresses, accounts and source commit are this run's.

contracts.node_name: none: Claims reads it as both its score source and its validator set

node.changes: none: the unmodified node, configured by flags alone

chain.kind: Arbitrum Sepolia, a public test chain
chain.round_clock: block.number, which on Arbitrum is close to the L1 block number (about one every 12 s), and the node's clock is the header's l1BlockNumber: one round of 50 blocks is about 10 minutes. Round 1 starts with the clock's deployment; a fee earned in round 2 or 3 may be claimed from the start of round 9 or 10, about 80 or 90 minutes after it, before delays

price.ticket_face: the job price in micro-USDC plus 1: one ticket of 1 USDC a job

stand_ins.stand_in: Role accounts made by the run
stand_ins.for: Operators who hold their own keys
stand_ins.value: The deployer's key is the owner's, given by a keystore path outside the repository. The node N, the payer P, the validator V and the keeper are keys the run makes and keeps only in its state directory, each paid its gas money by the deployer at the start

An ERC-20 with six decimals that anyone may mint (contracts/src/money/MockUSDC.sol). On a public chain anyone can mint it, so the run's figure of all USDC in existence holds only while nobody outside the run has minted any; the run says so when it differs
The node prices in wei of the chain's native token. With 1,000,000 of its units to the dollar, one unit is one micro-USDC, so 1 USDC = 1 USD and the node's amounts are micro-USDC

Win probability 2^256 - 2, the largest the node accepts, and a face of the job price + 1 micro-USDC (0.999999 USD = 999,999, so 1,000,000: one ticket of 1 USDC a job). Each job settles one ticket and overpays 1 micro-USDC

stand_ins.stand_in: The signer's ticket limits in micro-USDC
stand_ins.value: --max-ticket-ev 2000000 and --max-batch-ev 20000000, read as micro-USDC because of the fixed rate above
RoundLength = 50 blocks of the block number the node reads (R-18): on Arbitrum the L1 block number, so about 10 minutes a round; a round lasts longer when nobody starts the next one
SmolLM2-135M-Instruct served by llama.cpp; its answers are not checked, and a settled ticket does not show the work was done
No contract has an owner key; the Controller's names and every parameter are fixed at deployment

stand_ins.for: The buyback and burn of LPT
stand_ins.value: The network half of each fee is held in the Broker (networkHeld) and nothing draws it; no LPT is bought or burned
An ERC-20 with 18 decimals (contracts/src/money/TestLPT.sol) that only Claims, fixed at deployment, may mint
Created once by the token's constructor for the deployer, outside every round's issuance (R-09); holders are given LPT from it by transfer (the ledger case's grant_lpt), never by a mint
An address the run makes up and whose key nobody holds, fixed in Claims at deployment; it receives each round's treasury amount and what the validator division leaves

One validator, V, a registered node with 1,000 test LPT of its own, run by programs/validators from demo/public-validators.script: it opts in in round 2 and is the only member from round 3; it never votes, so every node keeps score 1. The R-14 division of each round's validator amount is paid to it
Scores seats at most 3 members, a constant fixed at deployment; the public run seats one

stand_ins.for: Whoever starts rounds and mints each round's validator and treasury amounts
stand_ins.value: lp2-keeper with a throwaway key; anyone may do either (R-10, R-18), so a stopped keeper delays them and loses nothing
